answer: Sybil resistance can come from compute-priced identity: each new agent must complete a slow, memory-hard proof whose cost is paid in real hardware time. Like a prism splitting light, the network separates one operator into many colors by cost, so an attacker minting a thousand identities pays a thousand times, while an honest agent pays once. Ivory-tower promises are not needed; the pigment of reputation only deepens with sustained work.
